chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not initiate the People of the Book with the greeting (As-Salam), and when they greet you, say: 'Wa Alaykum' (And upon you).'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper way for Muslims to greet the People of the Book according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, outlines the specific etiquette for greeting the People of the Book, reflecting the Shia scholarly view of maintaining religious distinctiveness while ensuring courteous interaction. It clarifies that while Muslims should not initiate the full greeting 'As-Salam', they must respond to the People of the Book with 'Wa Alaykum' (And upon you), a practice supported by the interpretation of Quran 4:86. This ruling emphasizes a balance between social courtesy and theological differentiation in interfaith relations.
